name: H.E.S.S.
notes: Derived lists (site_ids, detector_ids, document_ids, result_ids) are not stored in this record; they are derived from the other records.

The collaboration's About, Telescopes and Site pages (Internet Archive captures of April-July 2026, read 2026-10-25) do not give the commissioning date of CT5 (H.E.S.S. II), so none is recorded. A Max Planck Society article dated 4 October 2012 (mpg.de/6373837) reports the first light of the 28 m telescope on 26 July; it is not a collaboration source and is not recorded as the commissioning date.
No results or technical documents are recorded for H.E.S.S. yet.
H.E.S.S. II (the 28 m CT5 telescope) is part of the array per the official site, but no collaboration source consulted gives the date of its inauguration, so no interval is recorded for it.

summary.plain: Five telescopes on a Namibian farm that watch the southern sky for gamma rays: four medium telescopes plus one giant 28-metre telescope, the largest of its kind, run by scientists from more than a dozen countries.
summary.technical: High Energy Stereoscopic System: hybrid array of four 12 m and one 28 m imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes at 1800 m altitude in the Khomas Highland, Namibia. First light 2002; the collaboration's About, Telescopes and Site pages (Internet Archive captures, read 2026-10-25) do not give the commissioning date of the 28 m CT5 telescope.

unique_capabilities.quote: it is the only system of its kind that employs telescopes of two different sizes ... The use of two different telescope sizes enlarges the sensitive energy range of the system, which is approximately 0.1 – 100 TeV
unique_capabilities.value: A hybrid five-telescope stereoscopic array: four 12 m telescopes plus a central 28 m telescope; the only system of its kind employing telescopes of two different sizes, which enlarges its sensitive energy range (approximately 0.1-100 TeV).
